title: Single-cell multiomics reveals disrupted glial gene regulatory programs in Alzheimer's disease via interpretable machine learning.
authors: Zhang, Shuwen; Hu, Hongru; Wang, Xue; Xiong, Chengjie; Asmann, Yan W; Ren, Yingxue
journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
one_liner_zh: 该文通过单细胞多组学整合与可解释机器学习分析AD中胶质细胞调控程序，虽涉及转录因子调控但缺乏TF-DNA三维互作建模，方法可迁移至本课题。
abstract: Recent development of single-cell technology across multiple omics platforms has provided new ways to obtain holistic views of cells to study disease pathobiology. Alzheimer's disease (AD) is the most common form of dementia worldwide, yet the detailed understanding of its cellular and molecular mechanisms remains limited. In this study, we analyzed paired single-cell transcriptomic (scRNA-seq) and chromatin accessibility (scATAC-seq) data from the Seattle Alzheimer's Disease Brain Cell Atlas (SEA-AD) Consortium to investigate the molecular mechanisms of AD at a cell-subpopulation-specific resolution focusing on glial cells. We benchmarked various multi-omics integration methods using diverse metrics and built an analytic workflow that enabled effective batch correction and cross-modality alignment, creating a unified cell state space. Through integrative analysis of 26 human brain samples, we uncovered AD-associated gene expression and pathway changes in glial subpopulations and highlighted important transcriptomic and epigenomic signatures via functional inference and interpretable machine learning paradigms, discovering the profound involvement of the Solute Carrier proteins (SLC) family genes in multiple glial cell types. We also identified glial cell-specific regulatory programs mediated by key transcription factors such as JUN and FOSL2 in astrocytes, the Zinc Finger (ZNF) family genes in microglia, and the SOX family of transcription factors in oligodendrocytes. Our study provides a comprehensive workflow and a high-resolution view of how glial regulatory programs are disrupted in AD. Our findings offer novel insights into disease-related changes in gene regulation and suggest potential targets for further research and therapy.
abstract_zh: 单细胞技术在多个组学平台上的最新发展，为获取细胞整体视图以研究疾病病理生物学提供了新途径。阿尔茨海默病（Alzheimer's disease, AD）是全球最常见的痴呆形式，但其细胞和分子机制的详细理解仍有限。在本研究中，我们分析了来自西雅图阿尔茨海默病脑细胞图谱（Seattle Alzheimer's Disease Brain Cell Atlas, SEA-AD）联盟的配对单细胞转录组（scRNA-seq）和染色质可及性（scATAC-seq）数据，以细胞亚群特异性分辨率聚焦胶质细胞，探究AD的分子机制。我们使用多种指标评估了各种多组学整合方法，并构建了一个分析工作流程，实现了有效的批次校正和跨模态对齐，创建了统一的细胞状态空间。通过对26个人脑样本的整合分析，我们揭示了胶质细胞亚群中与AD相关的基因表达和通路变化，并通过功能推断和可解释机器学习范式，强调了重要的转录组和表观基因组特征，发现溶质载体蛋白（Solute Carrier proteins, SLC）家族基因在多种胶质细胞类型中的深度参与。我们还识别了由关键转录因子介导的胶质细胞特异性调控程序，如星形胶质细胞中的JUN和FOSL2，小胶质细胞中的锌指（Zinc Finger, ZNF）家族基因，以及少突胶质细胞中的SOX转录因子家族。我们的研究提供了全面的工作流程和高分辨率视图，展示了AD中胶质调控程序如何被破坏。我们的发现为疾病相关的基因调控变化提供了新见解，并提出了进一步研究和治疗的潜在靶点。
